lessons.title: What time is it?
lessons.scenario: Smarty and Mia check the bathroom wall clock before breakfast.

items.note: Ask 'What time is it?' when you want to know the hour.
Say 'o'clock' after a number to give the exact hour.
A clock shows the time on a wall or table.

image.describe: a round yellow wall clock with two black hands pointing to seven, no text

items.note: Say 'half past' before the hour to mean thirty minutes after that hour.

grammar.title: Telling the time
grammar.explanation: Start with 'It is' and add the number plus 'o'clock' for an exact hour, or 'half past' before the number for thirty minutes past.

practice.prompt: Look at the thing on the wall that shows the hours. What is it?
practice.explanation: A clock shows what time it is.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Use 'What time is it?' to ask for the time.

practice.prompt: The clock shows 8:00. Choose the best answer.
practice.explanation: Use 'o'clock' for an exact hour like 8:00.

practice.prompt: The clock shows 7:30. Choose the right time.
practice.explanation: 7:30 is thirty minutes after seven, so say 'half past seven'.

practice.prompt: Match the phrases that go together.
practice.explanation: Questions start with 'What time is it?', exact hours end with 'o'clock', and 10:30 is 'half past ten'.

practice.prompt: Ask Smarty for the time.
practice.explanation: Put 'What time' first, then 'is it'.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence for 6:00.
practice.explanation: Say 'six o'clock' for 6:00.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence for 9:30.
practice.explanation: Use 'half past' before the number for 9:30.

practice.prompt: Say the time aloud.
practice.explanation: Say 'It is half past seven' clearly.

turns.example: Yes, it is half past eight.
turns.hint: Answer Yes or No, or say 'It is half past eight.'

lessons.title: Morning routine
lessons.canDo: Say what you do in the morning

items.example: I get up at seven o'clock.
items.note: Say 'get up' when you leave your bed after sleeping.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat stretching happily as he gets out of a cozy bed in the morning

items.note: Say 'brush my teeth' when you clean your teeth.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat standing at a bathroom sink brushing his teeth with foam

items.note: Say 'take a shower' when you wash under falling water in the bathroom.

items.note: Use a towel to dry yourself after a shower.

practice.prompt: Smarty leaves his bed in the morning. Which phrase fits?

turns.hint: Say 'Yes, I brush my teeth.'

lessons.title: Every day
lessons.scenario: Mia and her father talk about school, work, and their daily schedule.

items.example: I brush my teeth every day.
items.note: Say 'every day' for something you do on all days.

items.example: I go to school every day.
items.note: Students say 'go to school' when they travel to their school.

image.describe: Mia and Sam the young cats walking happily along a path with backpacks toward a red school building

items.note: Use 'work' for the job adults do or the place they go to.

image.describe: a friendly adult cat sitting at a tidy desk with a notebook and a cup of tea

items.example: I get up at seven o'clock.
items.note: Put 'at' right before a clock time.

items.example: I take a shower in the morning.
items.note: Say 'in the morning' for the early part of the day before lunch.

grammar.title: at + time, in the morning
grammar.explanation: Use 'at' before an exact clock time (at eight o'clock), and use 'in the morning' for the part of the day.
examples: I go to school at eight o'clock.
We have breakfast in the morning.

practice.prompt: Which small word goes before 'eight o'clock'?
practice.explanation: Use 'at' before clock times: at eight o'clock.

practice.prompt: Mia is a young student. Where does she go in the morning?
practice.explanation: Students go to school; adults go to work.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I go to school in the morning.
practice.answer: I go to school in the morning.
options: I go to school in the morning.
I go to work every day.
I get up at seven o'clock.
practice.explanation: The sentence ends with 'in the morning'.

practice.prompt: Match the two halves of each phrase.
practice.explanation: These are key time and routine phrases: at seven o'clock, in the morning, go to school, every day.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about your father.
practice.answer: My father goes to work every day.
practice.explanation: With 'My father' (he), use 'goes to work'.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence with the right word.
practice.text: I get up ___ half past six.
practice.explanation: Use 'at' before 'half past six'.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: Breakfast is in the morning.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: I go to school at eight o'clock.
practice.answer: I go to school at eight o'clock.
practice.explanation: Use 'at' before 'eight o'clock'.

image.describe: Mia the young cat with her school bag waving goodbye to her father cat in a work tie at the front door while Smarty watches.

lines.text: Yes! I go to school every day in the morning.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: What time do you go to school?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: I go to school at eight o'clock.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: And your father?

lines.speaker: Mia
lines.text: My father goes to work at eight o'clock too!

questions.prompt: When does Mia go to school?
questions.explanation: Mia says: I go to school every day in the morning.

questions.prompt: What does Mia's father do at eight o'clock?
questions.explanation: Mia says: My father goes to work at eight o'clock too!

mission.setup: Smarty asks about your morning schedule.

turns.smarty: What time do you get up in the morning?
accept: ^i get up at (?:five|six|seven|eight|nine|ten) oclock(?: in the morning)?$
turns.example: I get up at seven o'clock in the morning.
turns.hint: Say 'I get up at...' and an hour.

turns.smarty: Do you go to school every day?
turns.example: Yes, I go to school every day.
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, I go to school every day.' or 'No, I go to work every day.'

lessons.title: She gets up early
lessons.scenario: Smarty compares Zara's early morning habits with Leo's habits.

items.example: I usually get up at seven o'clock.
items.note: Say 'usually' for something that happens most days.
Say 'always' for something you do every single time, 100%.
Say 'never' for something that does not happen at all, 0%.

items.example: I sometimes have eggs for breakfast.
items.note: Say 'sometimes' for something you do once in a while, not every day.
Say 'early' when something happens near the start of the day or before the usual time.

grammar.title: he / she + -s, and how often
grammar.explanation: Add -s or -es to the verb after he or she (she gets up, he brushes, he goes). Put words like always, usually, sometimes, and never right before the action.
examples: He never has tea for breakfast.

practice.prompt: Zara brushes her teeth 7 days out of 7. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: 'Always' means 100% of the time.

practice.prompt: Smarty is a cat, so he goes to school 0 days. Which word fits?
practice.explanation: 'Never' means 0% of the time.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: With 'She', use 'gets up', and 'early' comes at the end.

practice.prompt: Match the words with their meaning.
practice.explanation: 'Always' is every day, 'never' is zero days, and six o'clock is early.

practice.prompt: Put the words in order.
practice.answer: He usually takes a shower in the morning.
practice.explanation: 'Usually' goes before 'takes a shower', and 'takes' ends in -s for 'He'.

practice.prompt: Leo has juice only two mornings a week. Complete the sentence.
practice.explanation: 'Sometimes' means once in a while, not every day.

practice.prompt: Choose the right verb form after 'She'.
practice.explanation: After 'She', add -s: 'gets up'.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.explanation: Say 'She always gets up early.'

turns.example: I usually get up early.

turns.smarty: Do you always take a shower in the morning?
accept: ^(?:yes )?i (?:always|usually|sometimes|never) take a shower(?: in the morning)?$
turns.example: Yes, I always take a shower in the morning.
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, I always take a shower in the morning.' or use usually/sometimes/never.

lessons.title: Days of the week
lessons.scenario: Ana and Smarty check the school days from Monday to Friday.

items.note: Monday is the first school or work day of the week.

items.example: Every Tuesday, I go to school.
items.note: Tuesday is the second day of the school week, right after Monday.
Wednesday is the middle day of the school week.

items.example: Every Thursday, she gets up early.
items.note: Thursday is the fourth day of the school week, between Wednesday and Friday.
Friday is the fifth day of the school week.

grammar.title: Capital letters for days
grammar.explanation: Always start every day of the week with a capital letter: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday.
examples: Every Friday, we have fish for lunch.

practice.prompt: Which day is day one of the school week?
practice.explanation: Monday is the first day of the school week.

practice.prompt: Monday, Tuesday, ___, Thursday, Friday. Which day is missing?
practice.explanation: Wednesday comes between Tuesday and Thursday.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.explanation: Smarty says 'It is Thursday.'

practice.prompt: Match the school days with their order.
practice.explanation: 1 = Monday, 2 = Tuesday, 4 = Thursday, 5 = Friday.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence.
practice.answer: Every Friday I have fish for lunch.
practice.explanation: Start with 'Every Friday' and keep the capital F.

practice.prompt: Complete the sequence: Monday, ___, Wednesday.
practice.explanation: Tuesday is day two, between Monday and Wednesday.

practice.prompt: Say the five weekdays aloud.
practice.explanation: Say all five weekdays in order.

story.hook: Why is Ana so happy about Friday?

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Friday! I go to school Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Every Friday, we have delicious cake at lunch!

lines.speaker: Ana
lines.text: Yes! Friday is my best day!

questions.prompt: What day is it in the story?

questions.prompt: What do Smarty and Ana have at lunch every Friday?

turns.smarty: Do you go to school every Friday?

lessons.title: The weekend

items.note: Saturday is the day after Friday and the start of the weekend.

items.example: Every Sunday, we have a big breakfast.
items.note: Sunday is the day after Saturday and the second day of the weekend.

items.example: Saturday and Sunday are the weekend.
items.note: The weekend is Saturday and Sunday together, when most people rest.
Use 'sleep' when you close your eyes and rest in bed.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat curled up peacefully asleep on a soft pillow

items.note: Say 'late' when something happens after the usual time, like sleeping until ten o'clock.

practice.prompt: Which two days are the weekend?
practice.explanation: Saturday and Sunday make up the weekend.

practice.explanation: Listen for 'sleeps late'.

practice.prompt: Match the words that go together.
practice.explanation: Saturday and Sunday are the weekend; 6:00 is early and 10:00 is late.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about Sunday.
practice.explanation: Keep the capital S in 'Sunday'.

practice.prompt: Complete the sequence: Thursday, Friday, ___.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.

grammar.explanation: Use 'Does' before he or she to ask a question. Keep the main verb simple (no -s): 'Does he read?' Answer 'Yes, he does.' or 'No, he does not.'
examples: Does she watch TV? Yes, she does.

items.example: I do my homework in the evening.
items.note: Homework is the school work students do at home after school.

image.describe: Ben the cat sitting at a table with an open notebook and a pencil doing schoolwork

items.example: We have dinner in the evening.
items.note: Say 'in the evening' for the late part of the day around dinner and bedtime.

practice.prompt: You have dinner at 7:00 PM and go to bed at 9:00 PM. This is ***.
practice.explanation: Dinner and bedtime happen in the evening.

practice.prompt: Ben is a student. He has school work to do in the evening. What is it?
practice.explanation: School work done after school is called homework.

practice.prompt: Listen, then choose what you heard.
practice.audio: I go to bed at half past nine.
practice.answer: I go to bed at half past nine.
options: I go to bed at half past nine.
I get up at half past six.
I go to school at eight o'clock.
practice.explanation: The sentence says 'I go to bed at half past nine.'

practice.prompt: Match each activity with the part of the day.
practice.explanation: You get up in the morning, do homework in the evening, sleep late at the weekend, and go to bed at nine o'clock.

practice.prompt: Build the sentence about Zara.
practice.answer: She always does her homework in the evening.
practice.explanation: With 'She', use 'does her homework' and end with 'in the evening'.

practice.prompt: Complete the sentence about Smarty.
practice.explanation: With 'Smarty' (he), use 'goes to bed'.

practice.prompt: Complete the question about Ben.
practice.text: ___ he watch TV in the evening?
practice.explanation: Use 'Does' to ask about 'he'.

practice.prompt: Say the sentence aloud.
practice.text: I brush my teeth and go to bed.
practice.answer: I brush my teeth and go to bed.
practice.explanation: Say 'I brush my teeth and go to bed.'

story.hook: What does Smarty do before he goes to bed?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat brushing his teeth in the bathroom at night while Ben the cat holds his finished homework notebook.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Good evening, Ben! What time is it?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: It is half past eight. I always do my homework in the evening.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: Does Zara do her homework in the evening too?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Yes, she does! And she usually reads a book.

lines.speaker: Smarty
lines.text: I brush my teeth at nine o'clock, and I go to bed!

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.text: Good! See you tomorrow!

questions.prompt: What does Ben always do in the evening?
questions.explanation: Ben says: I always do my homework in the evening.

questions.prompt: What does Smarty do at nine o'clock?
questions.answer: He brushes his teeth and goes to bed.
options: He brushes his teeth and goes to bed.
questions.explanation: Smarty says: I brush my teeth at nine o'clock, and I go to bed!

mission.setup: Tell Smarty about your evening and bedtime.

turns.smarty: What do you do in the evening?
accept: ^i (?:do my homework|read|read a book|watch tv|take a shower)(?: in the evening)?$
turns.example: I do my homework in the evening.
turns.hint: Say 'I do my homework in the evening.' or 'I read a book.'

turns.smarty: What time do you go to bed?
accept: ^i go to bed at half past (?:eight|nine|ten)$
turns.example: I go to bed at nine o'clock.
turns.hint: Say 'I go to bed at...' and an hour.

turns.smarty: Does Smarty go to bed early?
turns.example: Yes, he goes to bed early.
turns.hint: Say 'Yes, he does.' or 'Yes, he goes to bed early.'

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Good evening! It is half past nine. I brush my teeth and go to bed.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat yawning in his cozy bedroom next to a big round clock showing 9:30.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: I always sleep early, and I get up at seven o'clock every Monday.

image.describe: Smarty the black cat tucked under a warm blanket with his eyes closed peacefully.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: Smarty! Get up! It is Monday!

image.describe: Mia the cat standing at the bedroom doorway holding her school backpack in the bright morning light.
Smarty the black cat rubbing his eyes in bed and looking toward the wall clock.

panels.speaker: Mia
panels.text: See the clock! It is half past eight! I go to school at eight o'clock!

image.describe: A close view of the round wall clock showing 8:30 while Mia looks surprised.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Oh no! I take a shower and brush my teeth! Where is my towel?

image.describe: Smarty the black cat rushing into the bathroom holding a green toothbrush.

panels.speaker: Sam
panels.text: Mia! Smarty! It is not Monday! It is Sunday! It is the weekend!

image.describe: Sam the cat laughing in the hallway holding a big Sunday pancake breakfast plate.

panels.speaker: Smarty
panels.text: Sunday! We do not go to school! But where is our big clock?

image.describe: Smarty, Mia, and Sam looking up in surprise at an empty hook on the wall where the clock was.

questions.prompt: What day does Mia think it is?
questions.explanation: Mia says: Smarty! Get up! It is Monday!

questions.prompt: What day is it really?
questions.explanation: Sam says: It is not Monday! It is Sunday! It is the weekend!

questions.prompt: What is missing at the end of the episode?
questions.explanation: Smarty asks: But where is our big clock?
